title: Build a modifier group the Aloha way (groups are items; 10 per item, 54 per group)
summary: Creates the group and its limits in the workbench, then mirrors Aloha record construction: modifier items exist first, the group collects them, and the item attaches up to ten groups on its Modifier tab. Menu-wide sharing stays confined to exception modifier groups.

inputs.name: memberItem
inputs.description: first member only — an Aloha group is a collection of item records, so a group with no members is not a real record; add the rest in Maintenance > Menu > Modifier Groups

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: comma- or semicolon-separated; each must be an item on this location's menu

steps.title: Create or update the modifier group with its selection limits
Give the group its first member item
Attach the group to its items in the workbench
notes: soft by design: items that do not exist in this menu are a no-op, not a failure

steps.title: Create the modifier items first, then collect them into the group
steps.instructions: Maintenance > Menu > Items defines the items (cheese, lettuce, pickles); Maintenance > Menu > Modifier Groups collects them (Extras) and the item attaches them back. A group that is never assigned to an item on its Modifier tab does not appear at the terminal - and an item can take at most ten groups (Modifier 1 through Modifier 10, Standard type only).

steps.title: Set the layout, prompting and free allowance
steps.instructions: Up to 54 modifiers per group; buttons show the short name, item number and price. Choose whether the group appears automatically or via the Modify button, set min/max (1/1 for a forced single choice), and set Free for the number of no-charge selections.

steps.title: Keep menu-wide sharing inside an exception modifier group
steps.instructions: For things like hot sauce or cheese sauce that modify anything on the submenu, use Maintenance > Menu > Exception Modifiers (reached at the POS via Modify > Special). That is the documented, intentional sharing mechanism - it is not the cross-contamination defect, and the audit allowlist treats it as designed sharing.

steps.title: Confirm the group this run built is actually populated
